AT0054.title: System/Application Vulnerability Exploitation Tools
AT0054.description: Vulnerability exploitation tools are software or hardware tools that deliver attack payloads against known security vulnerabilities in computer systems or network services. Their core capability is exploiting vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access, execute arbitrary code, or take control of a system. These tools focus on exploitation: building EXPs for memory-corruption vulnerabilities (buffer overflow, UAF, heap overflow), delivering payloads for web application vulnerabilities (RCE, SQLi, deserialization), local privilege-escalation exploits, and orchestrating modular exploit frameworks. They are commonly used for initial foothold, lateral movement, and privilege escalation in real attack chains. Vulnerability discovery (scanning, mining) is an upstream activity handled by dedicated vulnerability scanners and fuzzing/mining tools, and is out of scope for this tool.

AT0054-001.title: CI/CD Credential Scanning and Poisoning Tool
AT0054-001.description: Toolsets for finding pipeline credentials, modifying build scripts, or injecting malicious code into artifacts. Attackers scan code repositories and configurations for leaked tokens, AK/SK pairs, and key files, then use the obtained CI/CD pipeline permissions to tamper with build scripts, plant backdoors, or bundle malicious code into artifacts, so that all downstream services deploying those artifacts are infected at deployment time, achieving supply-chain-level lateral spread and persistence.
keywords: CI/CD Credential Scanning and Poisoning Tool

AT0054-002.title: Cloud Configuration Scanning and Key Abuse Tool
AT0054-002.description: Tools for enumerating cloud resources, detecting public storage, exploiting leaked keys, and moving laterally. Attackers scan object storage, API gateways, and IAM policies to find misconfigurations and public buckets, then use AK/SK pairs leaked from code repositories, logs, or environment variables to log into cloud consoles, call cloud service APIs to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally across accounts and regions.

references.title: Pacu: The Open Source AWS Exploitation Framework
CloudSploit by Aqua - Open-source cloud security posture management

keywords: Cloud Configuration Scanning and Key Abuse Tool

AT0054-003.title: Data Export and DLP Bypass Tool
AT0054-003.description: Tools for bulk-exporting collaboration documents, splitting archives, bypassing watermarking, and evading outbound audits. Attackers use automation scripts to bulk-pull sensitive data from mailboxes, drives, and databases, then split and compress it, strip watermarks and metadata, and exfiltrate it through multiple channels to evade DLP content inspection and traffic auditing, enabling large-scale data theft and exfiltration.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol (T1048)
MITRE ATT&CK: Data Loss Prevention Mitigation (M1057)

keywords: Data Export and DLP Bypass Tool

AT0054-004.title: MFA Bombing and Session Hijacking Tool
AT0054-004.description: Tools for MFA fatigue attacks, cookie theft, token replay, and session takeover. Attackers continuously push large volumes of second-factor verification requests to create fatigue and trick users into approving them, or steal browser cookies and session tokens for replay, bypassing MFA to take over accounts, often combined with phishing and man-in-the-middle proxies for long-term account persistence.
keywords: MFA Bombing and Session Hijacking Tool

AT0054-005.title: CDN and Edge Configuration Attack Tool
AT0054-005.description: Tools for testing cache keys, header pollution, edge functions, and WAF rule defects. Attackers craft differentiated request paths and HTTP headers, exploiting cache key confusion, web cache poisoning, edge function injection, and WAF rule bypasses to make edge nodes return malicious content or bypass access control, enabling credential theft, business-logic bypass, and large-scale client-side attacks.
keywords: CDN and Edge Configuration Attack Tool

AT0054-006.title: Dependency Poisoning Toolkit
AT0054-006.description: Tools and methods for publishing malicious packages to open-source repositories (npm, PyPI, Maven, RubyGems, Go Modules). Attack techniques include: typosquatting (registering packages with names similar to popular ones); dependency confusion (exploiting priority vulnerabilities between internal and public packages); maintainer account takeover; and installation hook exploitation. Typical consequences include credential theft, reverse shells, and cryptocurrency mining.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK: Supply Chain Compromise - Compromise Software Supply Chain (T1195.002)

AT0054-007.title: Container Escape & K8s Attack Toolkit
AT0054-007.description: Attack tools targeting containerized environments and Kubernetes clusters. Key capabilities include: container escape via kernel vulnerabilities or privileged configurations; K8s API abuse through misconfigured RBAC permissions or exposed API servers; lateral movement via ServiceAccount tokens and secret leakage; and persistence through malicious CronJobs, DaemonSets, or Admission Webhooks. Representative tools include CDK, PEIRATES, and kube-hunter.
